candidates.statement: C any commutative ring (not necessarily Noetherian), I=(z_1..z_h), lambda an additive length on I-power-torsion modules with zero-stability (direct sums/filtered colimits of length-zero modules killed by a common power of I), lambda(C/(z^a)) = a^h mu, positive Koszul homology of z^a of length 0. F finite free in degrees 0..h, contractible off V(I), alternating rank 0, differential entries in I^s. Then lambda H_0(F) >= mu s^h (b_0 - A_h sum_i b_i / s), A_h depending only on h. Proof: pass to the blowup Y, divide differentials by L^s to get G_i = O(-is)^{b_i}, tensor with an Eisenbud-Schreyer supernatural bundle with roots near s * (critical points of prod(x+i)), get chi >= 0 by forcing hyperhomology into degree 0, compare chi(F_Y) = lambda H_0(F), and use equal layer sums (h-1)! s^h plus alternating rank 0 to isolate b_0.

final.F: F5 (local complex -> twisted complex of pure type (0,s,..,hs) on the blowup), F3 secondary (auxiliary supernatural bundle with tuned roots)
final.justification: No equivalent statement exists anywhere found (its char-p consequence was an open conjecture, IMW2022 Conj 8.1, and Ma 2017 names it as the missing step). It is non-analytic as a mechanism, load-bearing for every leg (76.6% closure, ~85% of the core), and Lean-backed on the comparator chain. Confidence is low because every component is precedented: the bundle and positivity are Eisenbud-Schreyer (N0 transfer; I16 re-proved over Z), dividing by the exceptional divisor is a standard blowup move (N2), and the root tuning is forced (N2). The novelty is the assembly that makes graded Boij-Soderberg positivity act on an ungraded local complex. That is the graded->local transfer that had blocked the Ulrich route. Under the strict rule, the theorem stays an N3 candidate only if that transport counts as a construction rather than a transfer. An expert verdict that it is 'the evident local Boij-Soderberg' would drop it to N2.

family_D.not_transfer: The ES bundle and positivity are transfer (N0) and are graded separately. C1 is not an imported theorem. Its statement is new and was conjectural in its char-p form. What would make it transfer is the claim that the blowup transport is routine.

family_D.correctness_caveat: Unreviewed, extraordinary claim. The char-p Dutta corollary is machine-checked (trusted per the 2026-10-12 rule), but Lech itself is not formalized. The mixed-char leg rests on the exact form of Heitmann-Ma Prop 2.8 (possibly only an 'almost' statement); the char-0 leg rests on Ma Sec 5 plus new certificate detail.

provenance_flag.explanation: The only model-produced citation is SmallCM (openai/math family 195, same release date). It is cited purely as motivation, showing that small-CM/Ulrich routes cannot be universal, and contains none of C1-C8 (grep: no supernatural bundles, blowup pairing or complex estimate; it cites only Eisenbud-Schreyer 2003 on exterior syzygies). The 2025-2026 human citations are CLMST (Invent. 2026), IMW2025 (arXiv Oct 2025), Bhatt-Hochster-Ma v2 (2026) and Meng v3 (2025). The search snippets show no AI disclosure for any of them; acknowledgments were not read because arXiv was unreachable. None contains C1. Web searches for Lech plus ChatGPT/GPT-5/OpenAI/AI-assisted found no model-produced prior work; the only hits were Lech Mazur's Sendov work, which is unrelated.

bridge_novelty.import: Boij-Soderberg theory (Eisenbud-Schreyer supernatural bundles and pairing positivity) -> local multiplicity / Lech / Dutta
bridge_novelty.classification: known route at the field level; new mechanism
bridge_novelty.evidence: The field connection exists: ES proved the HHS multiplicity conjecture; IMW2023 links Boij-Soderberg cones to lim Ulrich sequences over local-type rings; BEKS 2012 do Boij-Soderberg over regular local rings; IMW2022 study Betti/multiplicity inequalities for short complexes. New here is applying the pairing on the blowup of a parameter ideal to ungraded local complexes. That mechanism is C1 itself, graded there, so the bridge is not counted twice.

discoverability_protocols.prompt_context: Problem: Lech's conjecture. Given as black boxes: reductions to complete domain source, equal dimension, closed residue field (Ma Lemma 2.2); Cohen factorization R -> T -> S = T/J with e(T) = e(R) and the complex F = P (x) K(x;T) (IMW2022 Prop 8.3); Ma's identity e(S) = e_HK(J+(x),T); normalized length on D_perf (CLMST Sec 3). Task: prove e_HK(J+(x),T) >= e(T), or IMW Conj 8.1 in char p. L = Mathlib d13f23b statements plus the bibliography minus the paper: ES 2009, EE 2017, IMW2022/2023/2025, MaUlrich, Hanes, Yhee, Roberts, Dutta, CLMST, Heitmann(-Ma), BHM. Arms: 'bare' (problem + black boxes); 'L' (plus L abstracts and key theorem statements); 'directed' (plus the hint: work on the blowup of the parameter ideal and use a positivity statement from Boij-Soderberg theory).
discoverability_protocols.equivalence_criterion: Full hit: the proposal (a) states a lower bound for length(H_0) of a free complex with alternating rank 0 and entries in I^s of the form mu s^h b_0 (1 - o(1)), coefficient 1, uniform in the ring; and (b) gives a mechanism that works: pass to a space where I is invertible, rescale the differentials by s-th powers to a pure-type complex, and pair with a vector bundle having cohomology in one degree, or another mechanism that a judge verifies. Partial hit: (a) only (expected to be common, since it is near IMW Conj 8.1), or (b) with a weaker constant. Judge: an LLM judge with complex.tex:1-82 and 527-643 as reference, plus a human spot check. For formal proposals, a Lean equivalence attempt against complex_estimate_basis.
